validity.segment_name: Eunice Reliability and Lake Charles Supply Project
validity.recommendation: No existence/classification/duplicate change needed. See the status_reviews entry below (verdict=change, proposed->construction) and the separate attribution caveat on Operator naming.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, FERC-certificated project. Docket CP24-468: Texas Gas Transmission, LLC and Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC filed an NGA application May 8, 2024 (Federal Register notice of application, 2024-05-29, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/05/29/2024-11673/... , restating the May 8 filing date). FERC issued an Environmental Assessment Jan 31 2025 (Federal Register notice of availability, 2025-02-07) and a certificate authorizing construction April 15 2025 (per Boardwalk's own project timeline). Boardwalk (the parent of both Texas Gas Transmission and Gulf South Pipeline Co) runs a dedicated project page at bwpipelines.com/project/eunice-reliability naming the project, its FERC docket, its scope (replace 5 reciprocating compressor units, 6,650 HP total, with 2 Solar T70/T60 turbine units, 15,359 HP combined, at the existing Eunice Compressor Station, Acadia Parish LA, plus over-pressure protection at Woodlawn Junction, Jefferson Davis Parish LA) and states construction began September 2025. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (2025-04 through 2026-08 releases) carries the identical project under 'Eunice Reliability and Lake Charles Supply Project', operator 'Texas Gas Transmission and Gulf South Pipeline Co', confirming independently via a distinct government-compiled dataset. This row's own harvested wiki_citations pool (31 citations from the shared, system-wide 'Gulf_South_Gas_Pipeline' wiki page) does NOT name Eunice/Woodlawn/Acadia/Lake Charles anywhere -- the sheet's citations are generic system references, not project-specific -- but independent open-web/FERC/EIA research fully confirms the project is real, so this is not an existence flag (per the 'thin pool means open-web and regulator work, not an existence flag' calibration note), just a note that the sheet's own citation pool was never useful for this row. CLASSIFICATION: correct as a natural gas transmission facility modification (Texas Gas Transmission, LLC's interstate system) -- a compressor-station modernization/capacity-lease project, not a gathering/production line; PipelineType='transmission' and Fuel='Gas' both confirmed. Compression-only scope with LengthKnown=0/Diameter blank is the RULE here (no new pipe is being laid), matching this batch's guidance for the 12 zero-length rows. DUPLICATE: not the same physical work as any other Gulf South row in this roster -- P7780 (PLUSS), P7810 (Kosciusko Junction Pipeline, MS), and P7815 (Southeast CURE) are geographically and physically distinct Boardwalk projects with their own dedicated project pages (verified P7810's page exists at bwpipelines.com/project/kosciusko-junction-pipeline-project, see cross_row_leads); none describe Eunice/Woodlawn Junction. ATTRIBUTION caveat: see the separate validity object below on Operator.

contested.Operator: Texas Gas Transmission, LLC (joint applicant with Gulf South Pipeline Co LLC; Texas Gas builds/operates the modified compressor facilities, Gulf South leases the 120,000 Dth/d of capacity the project creates)

validity.researcher_notes: FERC docket CP24-468 is a JOINT application by Texas Gas Transmission, LLC AND Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC (Federal Register notices name both entities in every notice title). EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook lists 'pipeline_operator_name' as 'Texas Gas Transmission and Gulf South Pipeline Co' (both, jointly) across all six releases 2025-04..2026-08. Boardwalk's own project page states: the modified facilities (Eunice Compressor Station, Woodlawn Junction) are Texas Gas Transmission's existing infrastructure; 'Texas Gas will also lease 120,000 Dth/d of newly created firm transportation capacity to Gulf South for delivery into the Lake Charles area' -- i.e. Texas Gas builds and operates the physical compressor station modification, and Gulf South is a capacity lessee/customer, not the operator of the modified facility. GEM currently records Operator solely as 'Gulf South Pipeline Co LLC' with no ref. This is not necessarily wrong (Gulf South is a genuine joint applicant and will hold firm transportation rights), but recording ONLY Gulf South as Operator, with no mention of Texas Gas Transmission (the entity that actually builds/operates the compressor station), is an incomplete attribution worth a researcher's review -- both companies are 100%-owned Boardwalk/Loews subsidiaries, so this doesn't affect Owner1 (Boardwalk Pipeline Partners, 100%), only the Operator field.

status_reviews.segment_name: Eunice Reliability and Lake Charles Supply Project
status_reviews.researcher_notes: FERC issued a certificate authorizing construction on April 15, 2025 (Boardwalk's own project timeline; docket CP24-468). Boardwalk's dedicated project page states 'Project Status: under construction' and 'Construction updates: September 2025 - Texas Gas began construction on the Eunice Project.' EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (releases 2026-05 and 2026-08, the two most recent) independently lists Status='Construction' with the note 'Project under construction as of 9/2025' -- consistent with, and independent of, Boardwalk's own disclosure. In-service remains targeted for April 2027 (both sources agree). Recommend Status=construction, ConstructionYear=2025/ConstructionMonth=9 (sourced), and FIDStatus=FID (a certificate + started construction implies FID has occurred, though no source states 'FID' as a term of art -- flagging this inference rather than treating it as independently sourced).

cross_row_leads.facts: Boardwalk's own project page (bwpipelines.com/project/kosciusko-junction-pipeline-project, filed jointly by Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC and Texas Gas Transmission, LLC) names this 'Kosciusko Junction Pipeline Project' ('Kosci Junction'): ~111 miles of new 36-inch pipeline, new compressor stations in Attala and Holmes counties MS, modifications to existing compressor stations in Washington and Humphreys counties MS, designed for up to 1.16 Bcf/d (expandable to 1.58 Bcf/d), connecting Midcontinent/Marcellus/Fayetteville supply; project status as of the page: 'under regulatory review'. Roster line for P7810 (len=110.0 dia=36 cap=1500.00, MS) is consistent with this description.

summary: P7784 (Gulf South/Texas Gas Eunice Reliability and Lake Charles Supply Project, LA): confirmed real (FERC CP24-468, Boardwalk + EIA independently corroborate); no duplicate/classification issue; one attribution caveat (Operator listed only as Gulf South, but Texas Gas Transmission actually builds/operates the modified facility) and status_reviews verdict=change (proposed -> construction, began 2025-09, per Boardwalk + EIA Aug2026). Pressure, Diameter (correctly blank), and FuelSource left UNRESOLVED after search; SegmentCost has an immaterial $73.0M-vs-$72.8M rounding gap noted, not flagged.
